BiblicalUsage: In Scripture, geresh means a thing put forth, yield, produce, thing thrust forth. It occurs just once, in Deuteronomy.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is simple here: geresh means a thing put forth, yield, produce, thing thrust forth, and I do not stretch it further.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
